desc: Redox-mediator flow cell whose dissolved shuttle charges and discharges a huge heap of raw mineral ore, so energy capacity separates from the stack
Oversized energy-intensive industrial plants run hard during surplus and idle during lulls, with energy "stored" as product inventory
Desalination splits water into fresh and brine ponds; pressure-retarded osmosis or reverse electrodialysis recovers the mixing energy
Electrochemically reduce CO2 into a storable carbon fuel (methane or formate), then oxidize it back to power and recapture the CO2 in a closed loop
Electrolytically or H2-reduced iron powder stored in piles, burned in air for steam power, with the rust re-reduced (metal-fuel cycle)
Thermochemical calcium looping: power calcines limestone, then CaO and CO2 recombine to release high-temperature heat for a turbine
Cheap sensible or latent heat storage (hot rock, sand, firebrick, molten salt, Carnot battery) with heat-to-power conversion
Compressed or liquefied air or CO2 stored in caverns, aquifers, domes or tanks and expanded through turbines
Gravity or pumped-hydro variants (underground or seafloor pumped hydro, rock-fracture or geomechanical pressure storage, weights in shafts)
Electrolytic hydrogen or ammonia stored in salt caverns or depleted fields and reconverted in turbines or fuel cells
Continental or intercontinental HVDC grids that smooth weather across uncorrelated regions, plus overbuild and curtailment, so less storage is needed
Ultra-cheap metal-air or rust-reversal batteries (iron-air, sulfur, zinc) built from abundant materials for multi-day duration
